subject: Crescent Health renewal: short-term price hold & accelerated upgrade plan
messages:
--- Message 1 ---
From: Danielle Park <dpark@crescenthealth.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Procurement <procurement@crescenthealth.com>
Date: Tue, 7 Sep 2027 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal & capacity bump — request for short-term price hold

Hi Jonas,

Quick note from our side: the pilot we ran with Redwood in Q2 exceeded expectations (lower latency, higher throughput), and our product team wants to accelerate the rollout into two additional regions for Q4. That means we are targeting ~30% uplift in committed usage for the next 12 months.

Procurement asked if Redwood can do a short-term price hold (60 days) while we close internal budget and PO approvals so we can lock the expanded commit at the current effective rate. If we can get a bridge price-hold + an uplift path, that will make the timing workable for us.

Two asks:
- Can you hold current pricing for 60 days while we finalize the PO?
- Can you provide a committed uplift offer (30% more commit) and any introductory credits or amortized onboarding credits to offset the initial ramp?

We want to move fast — available for a 30-min call tomorrow afternoon Pacific if that helps.

Thanks,
Danielle Park
Head of Platform Integrations
Crescent Health
[Attachment: usage_delta_q2_q3.csv (spreadsheet, 48KB)]

--- Message 2 ---
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Danielle Park <dpark@crescenthealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 7 Sep 2027 18:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal & capacity bump — request for short-term price hold

Thanks Danielle — great to hear the pilot performed well. We can absolutely work with Procurement to make the procurement window predictable. Two quick options we typically propose depending on how locked you want to be:

Option A — 60‑day price hold + staged commit uplift
- 60-day hold of current rates while PO completes
- Commit increase of +30% for a 12-month term starting on the PO effective date
- 1 month of credits (token-based) applied on the first invoice to offset initial burst

Option B — Short-term bridge + temporary accelerated discount
- 30-day price hold to allow PO issuance
- 6 months of a temporary 15% uplift discount on the incremental commit portion only
- Option to convert temporary discount into a permanent 6–12 month blended rate if commit sustained

I attached a quick pricing model with three scenarios so you can see invoice timing and credit impact. Can you confirm rough monthly consumption we should plan the model against? If you prefer, I can loop in Marissa and Finance for pre-approval on credits.

Best,
Jonas Weber
Account Executive — Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: pricing-model-crescent.xlsx (spreadsheet, 120KB)]

--- Message 3 ---
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Danielle Park <dpark@crescenthealth.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 8 Sep 2027 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal & capacity bump — request for short-term price hold

Danielle — looping in to confirm internal approval and give a concrete concession we can take to legal/finance. Appreciate the urgency; below is the proposal we can commit to today subject to final signatures.

Summary offer (Crescent Health — DEAL-4781):
- Price hold: Redwood will hold the customer’s current effective rates for 60 calendar days from the date of this email to allow PO and internal approvals.
- Commit uplift: Customer increases committed tokens by +30% over current baseline for a 12-month fixed term.
- Renewal discount: 12% discount applied to the base rate for the 12-month term once the PO is effective. Discount applies to committed usage only.
- Onboarding credit: One-time credit equal to one month of current average spend applied on first invoice to help cover ramp costs.
- DocuSign window: Crescent must execute the addendum within 90 days of PO issuance to retain the discount; otherwise standard rates apply moving forward.

Conditions & notes:
- The price hold is a temporary administrative measure; final billing will be determined by the executed addendum and PO effective date.
- Any usage above committed tier during the 60-day hold will be billed at standard overage rates and subject to normal reconciliation.
- This offer requires finance sign-off for the onboarding credit; Ben — can you confirm approval for the credit / accounting treatment?

Next steps proposed:
1) Jonah / Crescent: confirm the monthly usage delta and preferred effective date.
2) I will circulate a one-page addendum and a mutual action plan for sign-off (attached).
3) Legal/Procurement: review and route to DocuSign.

Attachments: crescent_addendum_draft_v1.pdf (addendum draft), mutual_action_plan.docx (M.A.P.), pricing-model-crescent.xlsx (scenario workbook).

If that looks acceptable, we’ll prepare the DocuSign bundle today and aim for signature within 7–10 business days.

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
VP, Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: crescent_addendum_draft_v1.pdf (PDF, 95KB)]

--- Message 4 ---
From: Danielle Park <dpark@crescenthealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@crescenthealth.com>, Michael Summers <msummers@crescenthealth.com>
Date: Thu, 9 Sep 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal & capacity bump — request for short-term price hold

Marissa / Jonas — thank you. The summary looks good and we appreciate the 60-day hold; that is sufficient to get the PO routed. A few clarifying points before we finalize:

- Confirm onboarding credit will appear as a line-item credit on the first invoice (we need this in the SOW).
- Can you confirm exact commit baseline numbers you used for the +30% calculation? We’ll validate against internal forecasts.
- Invoice timing: our finance team requires net-30 from invoice date; any changes needed on Redwood side?

Assuming those clarifications are included in the addendum, Crescent is prepared to sign. Please send the DocuSign link and routing instructions; Procurement will attach the PO number after signature.

Thanks —
Danielle Park
Head of Platform Integrations
Crescent Health
